gen_risks.description: Inadequate capacity of NAFIN and PFIs to design and implement sustainable finance products
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance and capacity building to NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN has limited experience in designing and implementing sustainable finance products

gen_risks.description: Limited access to long-term financing for SMEs and mid-caps
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide financing and co-financing options to SMEs and mid-caps
gen_risks.evidence: SMEs do not have adequate access to the loan products needed to invest in green technologies

gen_risks.description: Delays in project implementation due to inadequate capacity of NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance and capacity building to NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN's experience has mainly focused on overseeing and reviewing procurement processes

gen_risks.description: Limited participation of PFIs and beneficiary enterprises in the project
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage with PFIs and beneficiary enterprises through outreach and awareness-raising activities
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will channel financing through its existing network of financial intermediaries

gen_risks.description: Changes in government policies or regulations that may affect the project's implementation
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor policy and regulatory changes and adjust the project's implementation accordingly
gen_risks.evidence: The government has introduced policies and instruments to promote sustainable finance

gen_risks.description: Climate-related risks, such as extreme weather events, that may affect the project's implementation
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate risk management into the project's design and implementation
gen_risks.evidence: Mexico faces significant climate vulnerability due to its exposure to extreme weather events

gen_risks.description: Inadequate environmental and social risk management by NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide training and capacity building on environmental and social risk management to NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social (E&S) risk is assessed as Substantial

gen_risks.description: Inadequate governance and management structures within NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance and capacity building to NAFIN and PFIs
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN has a strong track record in implementing traditional, second-tier credit lines and guarantee programs

gen_risks.description: Economic downturn or crisis that may affect the project's implementation
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor economic trends and adjust the project's implementation accordingly
gen_risks.evidence: The project is expected to bring significant economic, financial, environmental, technical, and social benefits

gen_risks.description: Changes in global market trends or conditions that may affect the project's implementation
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor global market trends and adjust the project's implementation accordingly
gen_risks.evidence: The project supports Mexico's NDC 3.0 and the National Climate Change Strategy in both their adaptation and mitigation goals

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
